dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1810 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 1,858 items printed somewhere; by the finder's count 2 reach 11 papers, 3 reach 10, 16 reach 9, 21 reach 8 and 42 reach 7). The same script was run with year 1809 over the 1810 pages (items_from_1809.json: 279 items printed in 1810, 1 in 11 papers, 5 in 9, 11 in 8 and 13 in 7). Every item in 7 or more papers was read, and every item in 5 or 6 papers that a comparison of about 220 words of its text with every page put in more papers was checked. A sweep of the year for passages shared word for word (seven-word sequences) by 7 or more papers found short items that the reuse families had not joined, and those were counted too. Every item that might reach 7 was counted again by its own words, in both transcriptions, by phrase searches over all 3,933 pages of 1810 and by comparing about 100 words of its opening with every page, reading the hits.
dispositions.selection_rule: The one admission rule (R-01), as for 1776, 1800, 1802, 1803, 1804, 1805, 1806, 1807, 1808 and 1809: every single printed item in 9 or more newspapers is admitted, except digests; items in 7 or 8 papers are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news; items are counted one by one; a sub-story may have fewer papers when its parent reaches 7. No year-specific threshold: items of 1810 reach 7, 8, 9 and 10 papers. 9 or 10 papers are in print in any three weeks of the year (11 only in the weeks of the Martinsburgh Gazette's four issues), so an item in 9 papers was printed by every paper, or all but one, that survives for its weeks. Where several items of one affair reach the band in the same weeks, the most widely printed is chosen and the others are listed as not chosen, unless they are separate public acts (X-1800-01). Nothing is held back for its subject. 1810 is the collection's last year: only printings dated 1810 are counted.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1810 has 11 catalogue series, which are 11 papers; no paper appears under two catalogue numbers. The Delaware Gazette runs to 6 June, the Constitutionalist of Exeter from 21 May, and the Martinsburgh Gazette has four issues (27 July to 30 November). No 1810 issue has a corrected date, and the release's map of misfiled RevX pages lists none for 1810.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Counted item by item, eleven items of 1810 reach 9 or 10 papers and are admitted by the rule's first part: the President's proclamation of 2 November (10), the Treasury's circular of the same day (9), the President's message of 5 December (9), the Duke of Cadore's letter of 5 August (9), Mr. Pinkney's letter sending Lord Wellesley's answer on the decrees (9), Lord Wellesley's answer of 14 March on Mr. Jackson (9), General Armstrong's letter of 10 March with his letter to the Duke of Cadore (9) and his letter of 7 April (9), the letter from on board the Vixen (9), the Natchez report from Baton Rouge (9) and the letter from Washington, Mississippi Territory, of 30 October (9). 47 items reach 7 or 8 papers: 13 are chosen (Mr. Pinkney's letter of 2 January as a sub-story beside Lord Wellesley's answer), 33 are not chosen, and the National Intelligencer's paragraph on the Vixen is counted with the letter it introduces. Two sub-stories under West Florida are in 6 papers (C-01).
counted_item_by_item.Joins made by the finder: The finder chains the bills and acts on commercial intercourse, the President's proclamations and the Treasury's circular through their shared wording (the fourth section of the act of 1 May is quoted in the proclamation of 2 November and in the circular), the acts of the session through their enacting formula, the reports of the House's proceedings, and the documents of each publication of diplomatic correspondence. Each text was counted by its own words; only the act of 1 May reaches 7 papers by its own title among the acts of the session.
counted_item_by_item.Letters printed together: A letter and the enclosures printed with it are one item, counted by the letter's opening (C-03): Mr. Pinkney's letter of September with his note of 25 August and Lord Wellesley's answer; General Armstrong's letter of 10 March with his letter of that day to the Duke of Cadore. A publication of separate letters is counted letter by letter (R-01): of the despatches received by the John Adams, two letters reach 9 papers and fifteen are in 7 or 8; of the correspondence on Mr. Jackson's recall, Lord Wellesley's answer reaches 9 and Mr. Pinkney's two letters 8 each (X-1810-01).
counted_item_by_item.A letter counted across the reports that: The letter from on board the Vixen is printed after the National Intelligencer's paragraph in eight papers and with remarks of its own in the Rhode-Island Republican: counted by the letter, 9 papers (X-1803-02); the paragraph alone is in 8 (X-1810-02).
counted_item_by_item.Printed forms counted together: The French minister's note to General Armstrong of 14 February in three translations (4, 5 and 3 printings; 8 papers, C-02); the decree of Rambouillet as its own text or within a paragraph from the Bulletin des Lois (8 papers).
counted_item_by_item.Printed again counts again: The French minister's note of 14 February printed again in the government's translation in late May (ALX, VA, ENQ); the Duke of Cadore's letter of 5 August printed twice in the Rhode-Island American; the decree of Rambouillet and the Duke of Cadore's letter printed again in December, with the documents sent to Congress with the President's message (Enquirer, Norfolk Gazette); the declaration of West Florida printed again in December with other papers of the convention (C-08).
counted_item_by_item.Pages that only quote, summarise or reci: Not counted (C-07): the Delaware Gazette's summary of the committee of ways and means' letter on loans; comments on the King's speech that quote its passage on America (ALX, ENQ, April); the Portland Gazette's extract of the Treasury's report of December, which leaves out its opening (C-06); the Enquirer's and the Virginia Argus's paraphrases of the President's message of 3 January in February.
counted_item_by_item.Bills and acts: The act of 1 May 1810 is counted where it is printed under its own title (7 papers); Macon's bill no. 2, printed in April as reported and as ordered to a third reading, is not counted with it (X-1803-10).
counted_item_by_item.This year's printings: 1810 is the collection's last year: the President's message of 5 December and the Treasury's report of December are counted by their printings of December 1810; later printings are not in the collection. Items of 1809 printed again in 1810 are counted by their 1810 printings (C-11): the Secretary of State's letters to Mr. Jackson of November 1809 are in 4 papers in 1810.
counted_item_by_item.The resolution on General Wilkinson: The House's resolution of March 1810 for a committee to inquire into General Wilkinson's conduct (6 papers) and the same resolution offered again in December by another member (5) are two items, counted apart; neither reaches 7.

for_user_decision.Letters printed together: enclosures wit: As built (X-1810-01): a letter and the enclosures printed with it are one item, counted by the letter's opening (C-03); the separate letters of one publication are counted one by one (R-01). Of the despatches received by the John Adams, General Armstrong's letter of 10 March (with his letter to the Duke of Cadore) and his letter of 7 April reach 9 papers and are admitted; fifteen other letters and decrees of the publication are in 7 or 8 papers and not chosen. 1809 counted its December documents by the publication's parts instead (X-1809-01); counted that way, the French part of the despatches would be one group in 8 papers.
for_user_decision.The letter from on board the Vixen count: As built (X-1810-02), 9 papers: eight papers print it after the National Intelligencer's paragraph on the affair, and the Rhode-Island Republican with remarks of its own; counted by the paragraph, 8 (X-1803-02).
for_user_decision.The French minister's note of 14 Februar: As built (X-1810-03), 8 papers and 12 printings: two translations in April and the government's translation in late May, counted together (C-02, C-08).
for_user_decision.The act of 1 May counted by its own titl: As built (X-1810-04), 7 papers, the Enquirer's printing by its CA text, where RevX lacks the act; Macon's bill no. 2, printed in April before it passed, is not counted with it (X-1803-10).
for_user_decision.Two West Florida documents in 6 papers a: As built (X-1810-05): the declaration of the convention of West Florida (6 papers) and the President's proclamation of 27 October (6) stand under the West Florida story, whose Natchez report and letter of 30 October reach 9 (C-01).
for_user_decision.Mr. Leib's resolutions chosen for March: As built (X-1810-06): a senator's resolutions submitted for consideration (7 papers), labelled as a policy argument; no other item first printed in March reaches 7. Without them March has no story.
for_user_decision.Lord Wellesley's answer counted in a pap: As built (X-1810-07): the Delaware Gazette prints the letter whole, after satirical remarks of its own; a whole printing inside commentary counts (X-1802-04).
for_user_decision.Men named in the West Florida reports: As built (X-1810-08): the Natchez report names the leader of the party that entered the fort of Baton Rouge and the Spanish officers there; an armed rising against a foreign government's post is a public affair (X-1804-02).
for_user_decision.February without a story: As built (X-1810-09): no item first printed in February 1810 reaches 7 papers by its own words; the month's widely printed texts are bills and proceedings that do not.
for_user_decision.Grading calls on the transcriptions: As built (X-1810-11): graded fact-changing are RevX's '...' where the print goes on, a letter's dateline left out, an addressee line left out with a word misread, and a master's name read as a common word; graded minor are the label '(COPY.)' left out, 'Stirrup Key' for the printed misprint 'Stirrup Ray', 'Mian' for a faint 'Milan', a garble on a heavily inked print and letter-spaced transcription. '21 January' in two printings of Lord Wellesley's answer, where the figure is too worn to read, is not counted.
for_user_decision.A sweep for short items: As built (X-1810-10): the sweep of word-for-word passages shared by 7 or more papers (X-1803-09) was run for 1810; it found the Treasury's circular of 2 November and General Armstrong's letter of 7 April, both admitted, and several items listed as not chosen.
